content:
The next-generation iPhone lineup is about to launch, and it's going to be a different one. The base model iPhone 18 won't be making an appearance for now, as it has been moved to a spring release. This September, the spotlight will fall entirely on the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the all-new foldable iPhone.

Of course, the most obvious question in the market is the price hike. A price increase for the iPhone 18 Pro series is almost inevitable, which raises a question — is it wise to buy an iPhone 17 Pro at the current price?

What's new with the iPhone 18 Pro

The iPhone 18 Pro will be a minor upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro, though I don't think it qualifies as an "S upgrade year" at all.

Key new features include: a smaller Dynamic Island, a variable aperture main lens for finer depth-of-field control, a lineup of new colorways (including a red option), and Apple's first C2 modem for the Pro iPhone, which will also support 5G satellite connectivity.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max will be thicker and pack a larger-capacity battery; combined with the C2 modem, battery life is expected to see a significant improvement.

The chip side will also see the usual upgrades, including the A20 Pro (the first second-generation 2-nanometer chip) and the N2 networking chip. The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to retain the same 12GB of RAM as the previous generation. Apple will also redesign the Camera Control to reduce accidental presses.

Apple is likely to bring other surprise upgrades, but the above is what's known so far.

The price hike issue

This is the most controversial point. Apple has already significantly raised prices across the iPad and Mac lineup, and has signaled that further price increases are on the way. A price hike for the iPhone 18 Pro series is almost a certainty.

Exactly how much? It's hard to pin down. Some estimates suggest the increase could be as much as $300, though Apple may also reduce the hike by absorbing part of the cost itself. I expect the base iPhone 18 Pro to be priced somewhere between $1,199 and $1,399, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max between $1,299 and $1,499.

For most people, this will be a hard increase to swallow, especially since the new iPhone doesn't seem to bring a notable upgrade that matches the price hike.

Should you buy now?

Of course, it ultimately comes down to your personal decision. Personally, I think the iPhone 17 Pro will deliver an overall user experience on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, at a lower price. That really is hard to argue with.

Apple hasn't raised prices on the iPhone lineup yet, so you can still pick up an iPhone 17 Pro for $1,099 right now, or an iPhone 17 Pro Max for $1,199. If you're on an older iPhone and considering an upgrade, even though we're close to the new model's launch cycle, buying last year's model is still the smartest move.

The memory crunch triggered by AI data centers is expected to last for years, and Apple product prices are unlikely to come back down anytime soon. Please make your decision carefully.
